questions.question: Compare natural, semi-synthetic, and synthetic antibiotics. / [CO3, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Compare natural, semi-synthetic, and synthetic antibiotics.
  • Natural antibiotics are produced directly by microorganisms such as bacteria and
  • fungi; examples include penicillin from Penicillium and streptomycin from
  • Streptomyces.
  • Semi-synthetic antibiotics are derived from natural antibiotics that are chemically
  • modified in the laboratory to improve their effectiveness, stability, or spectrum of
  • activity; examples include ampicillin and amoxicillin.
  • Synthetic antibiotics are entirely man-made through chemical synthesis, such as
  • sulfonamides and ciprofloxacin. While natural antibiotic s are purely microbial
  • products, semi -synthetic ones combine natural and chemical methods, and
  • synthetic antibiotics are fully artificial, allowing greater control over their
  • properties and action.
  • [U] / [CO3, CO4]

  • changes in amplitude, which can be observed as differences in image contrast.

questions.question: Explain the steps involved in specialized transduction. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the steps involved in specialized transduction.
  • Specialized transduction is a type of bacteriophage-mediated gene transfer in which
  • a specific portion of the bacterial DNA is transferred from one bacterium to another
  • through a temperate phage (such as lambda phage in E. coli).
  • Phage infects → integrates into host DNA (prophage)
  • Faulty excision → picks up nearby bacterial gene
  • New phage carries bacterial DNA → infects another cell
  • Gene recombines → genetic change in recipient
  • [U] / [CO5]

  • chemical or physical agents that allow the enrichment or selection of one
  • organism over another. Pure culture isolation techniques such as streak

  • viability of pathogenic microorganisms present in a clinical sample and to
  • prevent the potential pathogens to be overgrown by other commensals or
  • contaminants in the specimen during the transportation of the clinical
  • specimen to the clinical/diagnostic laboratory.
  • Examples: Stuart’s medium, Amies medium, Cary–Blair medium, and Viral
  • Transport Medium.
